question: Gill sold two dogs at the same price. In one, he gets a profit of 22% and in the other, he gets a loss of 22%. What is Gill's profit or loss percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two items are sold at the same price with an equal percentage of profit and loss (x%), the transaction always results in an overall loss.

Overall Loss % = (x² ÷ 100) %

Here, the profit and loss percentages are equal, so x = 22.

Overall Loss % = (22² ÷ 100) % = (484 ÷ 100) % = 4.84%

**∴ The correct answer is 4.84% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Profit on Dog 1 = 22%

Loss on Dog 2 = 22%

Selling Price of Dog 1 = Selling Price of Dog 2

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = [100 ÷ (100 + Profit %)] × SP

Cost Price (CP) = [100 ÷ (100 − Loss %)] × SP

Loss % = (Total Loss ÷ Total CP) × 100

 
 Dog 1 (CP&sub1;)
 
 
 Dog 2 (CP&sub2;)
 
 
 Same SP
 
 

 

 
 + 22% Profit
 − 22% Loss
 
 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 

**Calculations:**

Let the Selling Price (SP) of each dog be 100 units.

⇒ Total SP = 100 + 100 = 200 units

⇒ CP of Dog 1 (sold at 22% profit) = (100 ÷ 122) × 100 = 10000 ÷ 122 = 5000 ÷ 61 units

⇒ CP of Dog 2 (sold at 22% loss) = (100 ÷ 78) × 100 = 10000 ÷ 78 = 5000 ÷ 39 units

⇒ Total CP = (5000 ÷ 61) + (5000 ÷ 39)

⇒ Total CP = 5000 × [(39 + 61) ÷ (61 × 39)]

⇒ Total CP = 5000 × [100 ÷ 2379] = 500000 ÷ 2379 units

⇒ Total Loss = Total CP − Total SP

⇒ Total Loss = (500000 ÷ 2379) − 200

⇒ Total Loss = (500000 − 475800) ÷ 2379 = 24200 ÷ 2379 units

⇒ Loss % = (Total Loss ÷ Total CP) × 100

⇒ Loss % = [(24200 ÷ 2379) ÷ (500000 ÷ 2379)] × 100

⇒ Loss % = (24200 ÷ 500000) × 100

⇒ Loss % = 242 ÷ 50 = 4.84%

**∴ The correct answer is 4.84% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Case of Same Cost Price (CP)

If two articles are bought at the same price and one is sold at x% profit and the other at x% loss, then there is strictly NO profit and NO loss overall.

Successive Discounts

When two consecutive discounts of a% and b% are applied on an item, the effective single equivalent discount is (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Dishonest Dealer Formula

If a seller claims to sell goods at Cost Price but uses a faulty weight, the Profit % = [(True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight] × 100.
